slides.title: El Clásico on Instagram: who won the content game?
slides.sub: What both clubs posted, and what stood out.

slides.title: ~2M likes on the full-time post
slides.body: “Full time at home.” Over 87k comments, and tagged as a Spotify paid partnership.

slides.title: ~1.4M likes with no caption
slides.body: A single 🥶 emoji and a tagged player, Mbappé, posted the day after.
slides.tip: Hypothesis: when the image carries the moment, fewer words can travel further.

slides.title: 18+ posts vs 9+
slides.body: Real Madrid published at least 18 #ElClásico posts. Barça, at least 9 in the same window, as visible on each grid.
slides.tip: Plan a full match-night grid, not one post.

slides.title: Feed posts beat reels
slides.body: At both clubs the top post was a feed post. Reels reached ~145k–230k likes at Madrid and ~520k–1M at Barça. Views aren't public, so reach is unknown.

slides.title: A highlight reel, a referee debate
slides.body: Under Barça's Fermín highlight, several of the top comments were about a Madrid player's missing yellow card, not about Fermín.
slides.tip: Before posting match clips, check what the comments will be about.

slides.title: Pre-plan match-night templates for win, draw and defeat.
Give each key player a quote or portrait post. Madrid did it for Lunin, Valverde and Mbappé.
